findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "naming-obviousness" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Reviews naming quality and code obviousness via the isolation test, scope-length principle, and consistency audit. Use when names feel vague, something is hard …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: naming-obviousness, red-flags, design-review, fetch-reference · Private data: code-evolution, red-flags, design-review, fetch-reference · Public sink: deep-modules.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: naming-obviousness, red-flags, design-review, fetch-reference · Private data: code-evolution, red-flags, design-review, fetch-reference · Public sink: deep-modules

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
